notes.title: Devlog #4, A new Look at The Mighty Eighth VR
notes.notes:
[p]Pilots, welcome back. This is our fourth devlog for [b]The Mighty Eighth VR[/b], and today we’re excited to share something short, sharp, and cinematic.[/p][p]We’ve prepared a brand-new teaser video that gives a taste of what’s coming - not a full reveal, but a snapshot of the atmosphere, the detail, and the immersion that define the Mighty 8th VR experience.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="owaX1Kvd6RU;full"][/previewyoutube][p]The footage is only 27 seconds long, but we think it captures the heart of what we’re building:[/p][list][*][p][b]The camaraderie of the briefing room.[/b] Next, we move inside, where officers lay out the day’s mission. Airmen sit in silence, focused on the map ahead. The player glances down at their own hands - a reminder that you are not just watching, you are [i]there[/i].

[/p][/*][*][p][b]The crew that makes it possible.[/b] On a corkboard, you’ll see the eight essential roles of a B-17 crew - from pilot and bombardier to radio operator and gunners. Every position matters. Every role is part of the story.

[/p][/*][*][p][b]The chaos of combat.[/b] Suddenly, you’re in the heat of it, manning a gun, tracking enemy fighters across the sky. Tracers cut through the sky. The responsibility of defense rests on you.

[/p][/*][*][p][b]The world below.[/b] Finally, a sweeping panoramic view. From low altitude, you take in the countryside below, rich with detail and atmosphere. It’s a world alive, and you’re flying right through the middle of it.

[/p][/*][/list][p]It’s just a glimpse, but it shows what we’ve been working toward: bringing the atmosphere, the scale, and the drama of the Mighty 8th to life in VR.[/p][p]We’ll have more to share soon - deeper looks at systems, roles, and how the co-op experience ties everything together. 
For now, enjoy this teaser, and imagine yourself in the thick of it.[/p][h2][/h2][p][/p][h2][b]A New Mission: The Bloody 100th Board Game Edition[/b][/h2][p]The B-17 story doesn’t just live on in the digital skies — it’s also coming to the tabletop.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121703/9f9d25d7fb37fe782e037f606990eb521ce64a37.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’re proud to announce [b]B-17 Flying Fortress: The Bloody 100th Board Game Edition[/b], a cooperative experience that lets you and your friends take command of a bomber crew during WWII’s most dangerous missions.[/p][p]Just like the video game series, every decision matters. You’ll chart courses, man the guns, repair damage, and push through flak and fighters to deliver your payload. Work as a team, or risk watching your Fortress fall apart around you.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="FUQTk3RpOug;full"][/previewyoutube][p]This board game brings the tension, camaraderie, and desperate heroism of the air war to life — with immersive scenarios, richly detailed crew roles, and a mission structure that will test your nerves from takeoff to landing.[/p][p]The project is heading to [b]Kickstarter[/b], and we want you with us from the very beginning. Visit our brand-new [b]“Notify Me” page[/b] to learn more and be first in line when the campaign goes live.[/p][p][/p][p]👉 link to the notify me KS page: [url="https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/microprose/b-17-flying-fortress-the-bloody-100th-board-game"]https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/microprose/b-17-flying-fortress-the-bloody-100th-board-game[/url][/p][p]

[/p]

notes.title: The Mighty 8th VR Dev Blog 3 – The Briefing Room
notes.notes:
Welcome to the third Dev Blog for “The Mighty 8th VR”.

In this blog we will be sharing developments on The Briefing Room, The Officers Club, Terrain, and a little bit more about our vision and what we are working on in the background.
[previewyoutube=6dCShMFACeo;full][/previewyoutube]
0:00 [url=https://youtu.be/6dCShMFACeo?si=d-_AxonKc5DbnE02]Briefing Room[/url]
1:03 [url=https://youtu.be/6dCShMFACeo?si=fsT_guYXJ0K_lt2t&t=63]Officer’s Club[/url]
2:12 [url=https://youtu.be/6dCShMFACeo?si=VWpjh9lQAJXmMS9w&t=132]Airfield[/url]
3:58 [url=https://youtu.be/6dCShMFACeo?si=OwQQ5C1G8aAN19nF&t=237]Terrain[/url]

[h2]The Briefing Room and Officers Club[/h2]
Currently we have taken some liberties and attached the Briefing Room to the Officer's Club at the end of a hall. This has been done to keep the idea of our virtual lobby together in one place without the need to traverse between areas and juggle scene loads when doing so.  However, this may change during development.

Our main goal is to create an immersive space where crews can actively plan out their roles and communicate amongst each other prior to deployment.  


[h2]Terrain[/h2]
Our environmental artists have been busy working on improvements to the airfield and the surrounding terrain. The video above shows the kind of detail we are currently achieving, and we can’t wait to show you some of your planned targets in future development updates. 

You will note roads, bodies of water and other features that will act as frames of reference for your navigator as your crew heads toward the target and back to the airfield.

[h2]Full Body IK work is in Progress[/h2]
We will share this in future dev blogs but one of our goals to keep you and your crew feeling immersed is to ensure we can show the full body and have that act correctly in different situations. We looked at the idea of just doing hands and heads like you see in some VR experiences, but we feel that may break immersion in this case.

[h2]Flight Gear[/h2]
The art team has been busy preparing some of the gear for the crew, and we are happy to share some of the work in progress below.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121703/32e1ed2e5810f69891d48066d3b540b31091e794.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121703/b6fc961130d7564c5c439a7b7b91db1c58610e12.png[/img]

Thanks for taking the time to read this far and we look forward to sharing more with you in the future.

notes.title: The Mighty 8th VR Dev Blog 2 - Test Flight
notes.notes:
Welcome to the second of our Dev Blog series for “The Mighty 8th VR”.

Today we are happy to share with you our further work in progress. 

[h2]Test Flight[/h2]

[previewyoutube=dSXVbhOnUiI;full][/previewyoutube]

We have aimed to create a sandbox and training areas around the Thorpe Abbotts airbase so players can test their skills and get some familiarity with guns prior to taking to the sky.

You will notice in the video that the airfield is starting to come to life. There are many vehicles moving from place to place and beyond. The keen-eyed among you will also notice a G506 driving around with a very interesting gun mounted on the back, whilst we don’t show you how this works in today's video it will come in videos further down the track.

The video also shows work in progress of some of the various roles that we have been implementing and testing. You will notice multiple gunner roles, pilot and bombardier roles are starting to take shape. Whilst we have been working on the Norden Bomb Sight, we felt it was better for us to save that for a future video. 

[h3]VR Notes:[/h3]
The video has been captured on a Steam PCVR build on an Oculus Quest 2 connected via wifi using Virtual Desktop. The game will also work via the Steam app and Oculus Airlink, using motion controllers. We have also been testing with hand tracking on the Quest 2, and that is partially working already.  We aim to support as many headsets as possible when the game launches.

[h3]Thanks for your support[/h3]
Thanks again for your support so far. The team is making great strides now as we have overcome some real technical hurdles we faced early on. We look forward to sharing more with you soon. 

Please feel free to reach out with comments and questions and we will see if we can cover them in future blogs. 

We are also avid VR gamers here, so if you have played an amazing VR game recently that you think our team should check out feel free to name-drop it in the comments.

notes.title: The Mighty 8th VR Devblog 1 - Driving to the Hardstand
notes.notes:
Welcome to the first dev blog for The Mighty 8th VR. 

This will be the first of many over the coming year. We will be sharing early footage of in-game footage as it evolves and welcome your feedback and suggestions. 

Within the VR gaming space, we acknowledge that there is a real desire to put the VR gamer first in order to truly craft a great experience. 

[b]Driving to the Hardstand[/b]

In this short video, you will see work-in-progress footage captured from a Meta Quest 2 via PC using Virtual Desktop.  We have tested the game with both Airlink and the new Steam app for Meta Quest, but during development, we find Virtual Desktop continues to be useful. 

This footage takes you from an area near Control Tower at Thorpe Abbotts down to the Hardstand where a B-17 sits with engines already running. 

We do drive dangerously close to the B-17, which is not recommended operation of a motor vehicle around an Aircraft preparing to taxi, but this was done for dramatic impact. In the final vision for the game, you will be starting each of the engines yourself before joining the Elephant walk to the runway, and we will share the progress we have made on that front in future videos.

Here is a brief overview of how interactions currently work within the Jeep.  You will need to grab the parking brake in order to release it, then grab the gear stick to put the vehicle in gear. Holding the right trigger will cause the vehicle to accelerate, whilst holding the left trigger will cause the vehicle to brake, in order to steer the vehicle you will need to grab the steering wheel with one or both hands.

[previewyoutube=fS2PaA7O3pU;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Thanks for your support[/b]

Thanks for taking the time to read this Devblog and we will be sharing early footage of the game as it evolves and welcome your feedback and suggestions.
